as_told.title: Matthew Brown and the Immaculate Constellation document on transmedium UFOs

plain: Matthew Brown, a former Defense Department official, is said to have found a document called Immaculate Constellation, about UFOs that move between air and water, wrongly uploaded to a shared government computer network called IntelLink. The filmmaker Jeremy Corbell tells Michels about the misplaced upload, and Michels, crediting Corbell and the journalist George Knapp, says the document talks about "transmedium objects, UFOs going in and out of the water," which would mean the government tracks such craft. The report itself is unsigned: the writer Michael Shellenberger gave it to Congress, Representative Nancy Mace entered it into the record of a House Oversight hearing on 13 November 2024 as coming from the Pentagon, Brown later said he wrote it, and a Defense Department spokesperson said the department has no record of a program by that name. It speaks of the capacity "to detect, track, identify, and engage anomalous transmedium platforms," which matches what Michels says, but it says only that its author "obtained access to this information while pursuing their lawful duties as an employee of the Department of Defense," so the shared server and the misplaced upload come from Corbell's account.

discussion.by: Immaculate Constellation report (anonymous, entered into the House Oversight hearing record, 13 November 2024)
discussion.text: An unsigned report that Michael Shellenberger delivered to Congress and Rep. Nancy Mace entered into the record of the House Oversight hearing of 13 November 2024 as a document from the Pentagon; it calls itself the public version of a Defense Department employee's report, cleared for release by the State Department; Matthew Brown, a former Defense Department official, later said he wrote it; and a Defense Department spokesperson said the department has no record of a program by that name. The report says of how its author came to the material only that they "obtained access to this information while pursuing their lawful duties as an employee of the Department of Defense", and it speaks of the capacity "to detect, track, identify, and engage anomalous transmedium platforms". The transmedium objects Jesse Michels mentions are in it; the shared Intelink server and the misplaced upload are Jeremy Corbell's account.
